answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity as stake plus endurance: every newcomer posts a bonded deposit that erodes toward its nadir across idle epochs and only returns to full weight at the zenith of sustained, verifiable work, while a small anchor committee of long-standing attesters must co-sign each enrollment so a fresh cluster cannot merely vouch for itself. Spinning up five hundred puppets then costs five hundred bonded, co-signed seats plus continuous labor to keep them ranked, which is more capital and effort than any single reward can repay.
